# Density contours {#sec-density-contours}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_bopit(
    base_size = 13))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_bopit()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_bopit()`, built from the Bop It toy: a deep purple background, a yellow frame and title, yellow, blue, green, orange, and pink marks, a purple to yellow continuous scale, and a Rockwell title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(faux)
make_group <- function(group, n, mu, sd, r) {
  faux::rnorm_multi(n = n, mu = c(bop_ms = mu[1], twist_ms = mu[2]),
                    sd = sd, r = r) |>
    mutate(age_group = group)
}
set.seed(1996)
bopit_players <- bind_rows(
  make_group("Teens", 150, mu = c(350, 400), sd = c(30, 35), r = 0.6),
  make_group("Kids", 150, mu = c(480, 560), sd = c(40, 45), r = 0.7),
  make_group("Parents", 150, mu = c(630, 720), sd = c(50, 60), r = 0.5)) |>
  mutate(player_id = row_number(),
         age_group = factor(age_group, levels = c("Teens", "Kids", "Parents")),
         across(c(bop_ms, twist_ms), round)) |>
  select(player_id, age_group, bop_ms, twist_ms)
# x limits
x_min <- min(bopit_players$bop_ms) - 50
x_max <- max(bopit_players$bop_ms) + 50
# y limits
y_min <- min(bopit_players$twist_ms) - 50
y_max <- max(bopit_players$twist_ms) + 50
labs_dnsty_2d <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  subtitle = "Milliseconds to respond to each command",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)"
)
ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    fill = after_stat(level),
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  # expand limits
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  # stat polygon
  stat_density_2d(
    geom = "polygon",
    color = "#23123F",
    linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  # gradient
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#5B2A9A",
    high = "#FFD400",
    guide = "none"
  )
ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill +
  labs_dnsty_2d
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ two numeric (continuous) variables**
:::

::::

## Description

Density contours (or 2-D density plots) are helpful for displaying differences in values between two numeric (continuous) variables.

In [topographical maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topography), contour lines are drawn around areas of equal elevation above sea-level. In density contours, the contour lines are drawn around the areas our data occupy (essentially replacing sea-level as '*an area without any x or y values.*')

Specifically, the contour lines outline areas on the graph with differing point densities, and semi-transparent colors (gradient) can be added to further highlight the separate regions.

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Install packages.


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_geom_density_2d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
install.packages("faux")
library(faux)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for data manipulation
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

*Bop It* (1996) shouted commands at you ("Bop it!", "Twist it!", "Pull it!") and sped up until you missed one. We'll simulate the reaction times (in milliseconds) of 450 players to the "Bop it!" (`bop_ms`) and "Twist it!" (`twist_ms`) commands. A player who's quick on one command tends to be quick on the other, so we'll draw the two times in pairs with [`faux::rnorm_multi()`](https://debruine.github.io/faux/reference/rnorm_multi.html). The `make_group()` function does this for one age group at a time, with its own means (`mu`), standard deviations (`sd`), and correlation (`r`). Teens are the fastest, parents are the slowest, and kids land in between. Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 450 players every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_geom_density_2d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
make_group <- function(group, n, mu, sd, r) {
  faux::rnorm_multi(n = n, mu = c(bop_ms = mu[1], twist_ms = mu[2]),
                    sd = sd, r = r) |>
    mutate(age_group = group)
}
set.seed(1996)
bopit_players <- bind_rows(
  make_group("Teens", 150, mu = c(350, 400), sd = c(30, 35), r = 0.6),
  make_group("Kids", 150, mu = c(480, 560), sd = c(40, 45), r = 0.7),
  make_group("Parents", 150, mu = c(630, 720), sd = c(50, 60), r = 0.5)) |>
  mutate(player_id = row_number(),
         age_group = factor(age_group, levels = c("Teens", "Kids", "Parents")),
         across(c(bop_ms, twist_ms), round)) |>
  select(player_id, age_group, bop_ms, twist_ms)
glimpse(bopit_players)
```
:::

## Distribution

A density contour is a map of where the points are crowded. Each contour line connects spots with the same density, like the lines on a hiking map connect spots at the same elevation. The Bop It data has three hills (one for each age group), and each hill has the shape of a bivariate normal distribution. Below we'll move from the players, to a picture, to the formula.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first two players in each age group.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_dnsty_2d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
bopit_players |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  slice_head(n = 2)
```
:::

Below we calculate the center, spread, and correlation for each age group.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_dnsty_2d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
bopit_stats <- bopit_players |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarise(mean_bop = mean(bop_ms), mean_twist = mean(twist_ms),
            sd_bop = sd(bop_ms), sd_twist = sd(twist_ms),
            r = cor(bop_ms, twist_ms))
bopit_stats
```
:::

The teens average about `r round(bopit_stats$mean_bop[1])` milliseconds to bop and the parents average about `r round(bopit_stats$mean_bop[3])`. The groups are far enough apart that they form separate crowds, but close enough that their edges overlap.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The graph below shows only the teens, with their points and their density contours. The contour lines are ellipses stacked inside each other, tilted because the two reaction times are correlated. The innermost ellipse surrounds the most crowded spot, right around the teens' means.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_dnsty_2d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
teens <- bopit_players |>
  filter(age_group == "Teens")
ggplot(teens, aes(x = bop_ms, y = twist_ms)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 1 / 2, color = "#1E90FF") +
  geom_density_2d(color = "#FFD400") +
  geom_point(data = filter(bopit_stats, age_group == "Teens"),
             aes(x = mean_bop, y = mean_twist),
             shape = 4, size = 5, stroke = 2, color = "#FF8C00") +
  labs(x = "'Bop it!' (ms)", y = "'Twist it!' (ms)")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

Each age group's reaction times come from a [bivariate normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivariate_normal_distribution). Its density (the height of the hill) at any point depends on how far that point is from the center, measured in standard deviations and adjusted for the correlation:

$$
f(x, y) = \frac{1}{2\pi \sigma_x \sigma_y \sqrt{1 - r^2}} \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2(1 - r^2)}\left[\frac{(x - \mu_x)^2}{\sigma_x^2} - \frac{2r(x - \mu_x)(y - \mu_y)}{\sigma_x \sigma_y} + \frac{(y - \mu_y)^2}{\sigma_y^2}\right]\right)
$$

Points where the part in square brackets takes the same value share the same density, and those points always form an ellipse. That's why the contours in **DRAW IT** are ellipses. With all three groups together, the density is a [mixture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture_distribution) (one third of each group's hill), which is why the graph at the top of the page has three peaks. The `level` values that `ggplot2` reports are these heights estimated from the data, in units of "players per square millisecond" (tiny numbers, because a square millisecond is a very small area). Try changing the kids' `mu` to `c(380, 430)` and two of the hills merge into one.

## Grammar

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

  - Create labels with `labs()`

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Create two values for extending the range of the `x` and `y` axis (`x_min`/`x_max` and `y_min`/`y_max`)

  - Map `bop_ms` to `x` and `twist_ms` to `y`

  - Add the `expand_limits()` function, assigning our stored values to `x` and `y`

  - Add the `geom_density_2d()`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_geom_density_2d
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: show
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
# labels
labs_dnsty_2d <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  subtitle = "Milliseconds to respond to each command",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)"
)

# x limits
x_min <- min(bopit_players$bop_ms) - 50
x_max <- max(bopit_players$bop_ms) + 50
# y limits
y_min <- min(bopit_players$twist_ms) - 50
y_max <- max(bopit_players$twist_ms) + 50

ggp2_dnsty_2d <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  # use our stored values
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  geom_density_2d()
# plot
ggp2_dnsty_2d +
  labs_dnsty_2d
```
:::


::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_geom_density_2d
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
# x limits
x_min <- min(bopit_players$bop_ms) - 50
x_max <- max(bopit_players$bop_ms) + 50
# y limits
y_min <- min(bopit_players$twist_ms) - 50
y_max <- max(bopit_players$twist_ms) + 50

# labels
labs_dnsty_2d <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  subtitle = "Milliseconds to respond to each command",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)"
)

ggp2_dnsty_2d <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  # use our stored values
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  geom_density_2d()
# plot
ggp2_dnsty_2d +
  labs_dnsty_2d
```

## More info

We're going to break down how to create the density contour layer-by-layer using the `stat_density_2d()` function (which allows us to access some of the inner-workings of `geom_density_2d()`)

### Base

  - Create a new set of labels

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Build a base layer:

    - Map `bop_ms` to `x` and `twist_ms` to `y`

    - Expand the `x` and `y` values with `expand_limits()` (using the values we created above)


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_base_layer
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
labs_sdens_2d <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)",
  color = "Age group"
)
# base
base_sdens_2d <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  )
base_sdens_2d +
  labs_sdens_2d
```
:::

### Stat

Add the `stat_density_2d()` layer:

- *Inside* `aes()`, use [`after_stat()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes_eval.html) to map `level` to `fill` (from Help, "*Evaluation after stat transformation will have access to the variables calculated by the stat, not the original mapped values.*")

- Set the `geom` to `"polygon"`

- Change the `color` to the dark purple background (`#23123F`)

- adjust the `linewidth` to `0.35`


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_stat_layer
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
stat_sdens_2d <- base_sdens_2d +
  stat_density_2d(
    aes(fill = after_stat(level)),
    geom = "polygon",
    color = "#23123F",
    linewidth = 0.35
  )
stat_sdens_2d +
  labs_sdens_2d
```
:::

### Fill

***Where did levels come from?***

*You probably noticed the `stat_density_2d()` produced a legend with `level`, and a series of values for the color gradient. These are the heights of the density 'hills' we described in the* **NAME IT** *section above (in players per square millisecond).*

Now that we have a color gradient for our contour lines, we can adjust the range of colors using `scale_fill_gradient()`

- `low` is the color for the low values of `level`

- `high` is the color for the high values of `level`

- `guide` let's us control the `legend`

We'll set these to purple (`"#5B2A9A"`) and Bop It yellow (`"#FFD400"`)

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_fill_layer
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
fill_sdens_2d <- stat_sdens_2d +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#5B2A9A",
    high = "#FFD400",
    guide = "legend"
  )
fill_sdens_2d +
  labs_sdens_2d
```
:::

### Points

The bright areas in the contour lines are the areas with higher value density, but why don't we test that by adding some data points?

  - Add a `geom_point()` layer

    - *Inside* `aes()`, map `age_group` to `color` (this will tell us if the three bright areas represent the three age groups in the dataset)

    - Set `size` to `2`

    - Change the `alpha` to `2/3`


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_points_layer
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# geom_point()
pnts_sdens_2d <- fill_sdens_2d +
  geom_point(aes(color = age_group),
    size = 2,
    alpha = 2 / 3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1E90FF", "#3CB043", "#FF5FA2"))
# final
pnts_sdens_2d +
  labs_sdens_2d
```
:::

We set the point colors with `scale_color_manual()` so they stand out from the yellow and purple fill.

## Even more info

In the previous plot, we used the `age_group` variable in the `geom_point()` layer to identify the points using color. In the section below, we'll show more methods of displaying groups with density contour lines.

### Groups

Re-create the labels

Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

Build a `geom_density_2d()` layer:

  - Map `bop_ms` to `x` and `twist_ms` to `y`

  - Expand the limits using our adjusted min/max `x` and `y` values

  - Add the `geom_density_2d()`, mapping `age_group` to `color`

Build the `geom_point()` layer:

  - Map `age_group` to `color`

  - set the `alpha` and remove the `legend`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_points
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
labs_dnsty_2d_grp <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)",
  color = "Age group"
)

ggp2_dnsty_2d_grp <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  geom_density_2d(aes(color = age_group))


ggp2_dnsty_2d_pnts <- ggp2_dnsty_2d_grp +
  geom_point(aes(color = age_group),
    alpha = 2 / 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  )

ggp2_dnsty_2d_pnts +
  labs_dnsty_2d_grp
```
:::

### Facets

  - Re-create the labels

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Build the base/limits:

    - Map `bop_ms` to `x` and `twist_ms` to `y`

    - Expand the limits using our adjusted min/max `x` and `y` values

  - Build the `geom_density_2d_filled()` layer:

    - Add the `geom_density_2d_filled()`, setting `linewidth` to `0.30` and `contour_var` to `"ndensity"`

  - Add the `scale_discrete_manual()`:

    - Set `aesthetics` to `"fill"`

    - Provide a set of color `values` (this plot needs 10 values, so we create them with `colorRampPalette()`, which blends the dark purple panel color into Bop It yellow)

  - Facet:

    - Add `facet_wrap()`, and place `age_group` in the [`vars()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/vars.html)

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_facets
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.8
labs_dnsty_2d_facet <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  subtitle = "By age group",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)"
)
ggp2_dnsty_2d_facet <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  geom_density_2d_filled(
    linewidth = 0.30,
    contour_var = "ndensity"
  ) +
  scale_discrete_manual(
    aesthetics = "fill",
    values = colorRampPalette(c("#2E1A52", "#FFD400"))(10)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(age_group))

ggp2_dnsty_2d_facet +
  labs_dnsty_2d_facet +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

Setting `contour_var` to `"ndensity"` scales each panel's density so its highest point is `1`, which is why every age group gets the full range of colors.

### Fill

In the previous section, we defined the color values used in `geom_density_2d_filled()` with `scale_discrete_manual()`. Below we give an example using the default colors:

  - Re-create the labels

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Build the base/limits:

    - Map `bop_ms` to `x` and `twist_ms` to `y`

    - Expand the limits using our adjusted min/max `x` and `y` values

  - Add the `geom_density_2d()` layer

  - Add the `geom_density_2d_filled()`, setting `alpha` to `0.8`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_fill
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
labs_dnsty_2d <- labs(
  title = "Bop It reaction times",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "'Bop it!' (ms)",
  y = "'Twist it!' (ms)"
)

ggp2_dnsty_2d <- ggplot(
  data = bopit_players,
  mapping = aes(
    x = bop_ms,
    y = twist_ms
  )
) +
  # use our stored values
  expand_limits(
    x = c(x_min, x_max),
    y = c(y_min, y_max)
  ) +
  geom_density_2d()

ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill <- ggp2_dnsty_2d +
  geom_density_2d_filled(alpha = 0.8)

ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill +
  labs_dnsty_2d +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")
  )
```
:::

### Lines

We can also outline the contours by adding color to the lines using another `geom_density_2d()` layer:

  - Set `linewidth` to `0.30`

  - Set `color` to `"#FFF6D6"`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_lines
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill_lns <- ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill +
  geom_density_2d(
    linewidth = 0.30,
    color = "#FFF6D6"
  )
ggp2_dnsty_2d_fill_lns +
  labs_dnsty_2d +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")
  )
```
:::
